subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Profit and Loss — Mark-up, Discount and Tricky Scenarios (W10 B2)

questions.stem: An item bought for ₹800 is sold for ₹950. Find the profit percentage.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Profit = 950−800 = ₹150. Profit% = 150/800×100 = 18.75%. Trap: 15.79% uses SP (950) as base instead of CP (800); 20% = 160/800 (applies 20% to wrong profit amount).

questions.stem: An article is sold for ₹640 at a loss of 20%. Find its cost price.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SP = CP×(1−loss%) → 640 = CP×0.8 → CP = 640/0.8 = ₹800. Verify: Loss = 800−640 = 160; Loss% = 160/800×100 = 20% ✓. Trap: ₹768 = 640×1.2 (adds 20% to SP instead of dividing); ₹720 applies 12.5% loss instead of 20%.

questions.stem: A trader marks goods 30% above cost price and allows a 10% discount. Find the net profit percentage.
questions.explanation: B is correct. Let CP=100. MP=130. SP=130×0.9=117. Profit%=17%. Short Trick: profit% = m−d−md/100 = 30−10−30×10/100 = 20−3 = 17%. Trap: 20% forgets the markdown on the already-marked-up price (miscomputes as 30%−10%=20%).

questions.stem: By selling 20 articles, a shopkeeper gains the SP of 5 articles. Find the profit percentage.
questions.explanation: C is correct. Selling 20 articles gives profit = SP of 5 articles. Let SP of each = s. Total SP = 20s. Profit = 5s. CP = 20s−5s = 15s. Profit% = 5s/15s×100 = 33⅓%. Short Trick: profit% = (number of articles gained/CP articles)×100 = (5/15)×100 = 33⅓%. Trap: 25% = 5/20×100 uses SP articles as denominator instead of CP.

questions.stem: A man buys eggs at 6 for ₹5 and sells them at 5 for ₹6. Find his gain percentage.
questions.explanation: C is correct. LCM of 6 and 5 = 30. CP of 30 eggs = 5×(30/6) = ₹25. SP of 30 eggs = 6×(30/5) = ₹36. Gain = 11. Gain% = 11/25×100 = 44%. Trap: 36% uses SP as base; 30% underestimates (mental arithmetic error).

questions.stem: An article is sold at 15% profit. If its cost price were ₹200 less, the profit percentage would be 25%. Find the cost price.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SP = x×1.15 (same in both cases). With CP = x−200: x×1.15/(x−200) = 1.25. 1.15x = 1.25x−250. 0.10x = 250. x = ₹2,500. Verify: SP = 2500×1.15 = 2875. New CP = 2300. Profit% = 575/2300×100 = 25% ✓. Trap: ₹2,000 assumes CP difference = profit difference directly.

questions.stem: A merchant sells goods at 10% loss. Had he sold at 20% profit, he would have earned ₹600 more. Find the cost price.
questions.explanation: B is correct. SP at 10% loss = 0.9CP. SP at 20% profit = 1.2CP. Difference = 0.3CP = 600. CP = ₹2,000. Trap: ₹2,500 uses 0.3CP = 750 (wrong); ₹1,500 uses 0.3CP = 450 (wrong difference).

questions.stem: Two articles are each sold for ₹990. One at 10% profit and one at 10% loss. What is the overall result?
questions.explanation: B is correct. CP of 10% profit article: 990/1.1 = ₹900. CP of 10% loss article: 990/0.9 = ₹1,100. Total CP = ₹2,000. Total SP = ₹1,980. Net loss = ₹20. Short Trick: loss% = (common%/10)² = 1%. Loss = 1%×2000 = ₹20. When same %age profit and loss occur, there is ALWAYS a net loss. Trap: 'no profit no loss' is the most common wrong answer.

questions.stem: A shopkeeper marks goods 40% above cost and gives a 20% discount. If the selling price is ₹560, find the cost price.
questions.explanation: C is correct. SP = CP×1.4×0.8 = 1.12×CP = 560. CP = 560/1.12 = ₹500. Net profit% = 12%. Trap: ₹450 = 560/1.24 (wrong multiplier); ₹525 uses 40%−20% = 20% profit formula (ignores compound effect).

questions.stem: A shopkeeper offers 2 articles free for every 10 articles purchased. What is the effective discount percentage?
questions.explanation: B is correct. Buyer pays for 10 articles but receives 12. Discount on 12 articles = 2 free articles. Effective discount% = 2/12×100 = 16⅔%. Trap: 20% = 2/10×100 uses the number paid as denominator instead of total received; 15% is a common rough estimate.
